s:
Consider the following statements about the new Consumer Price Index (base 2024):
1. CPI (Rural / Urban / Combined) is compiled by the National Statistical Office (NSO), MoSPI.
2. Its first release, on 12 February 2026, was for January 2026.
3. It has 12 divisions under COICOP 2018 and covers 358 items.
4. Food and beverages carry a weight of about 46% in it.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct (NSO, MoSPI; first release 12 Feb 2026 for Jan 2026; 12 COICOP-2018 divisions, 358 items, 12 online platforms added). Statement 4 is wrong: food and beverages weigh 36.75% in the 2024 series; about 46% was the weight in the 2012 series.

s:
Match List-I (Index) with List-II (Compiled by):
List-I | List-II
a. CPI-IW | i. Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT
b. CPI-UNME | ii. Central Statistical Office (CSO)
c. WPI | iii. Labour Bureau
d. Consumer Food Price Index | iv. National Statistical Office (NSO)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: CPI-IW – Labour Bureau (Ministry of Labour and Employment); CPI-UNME – CSO, the only one of the CPI-IW/AL/RL/UNME family not compiled by the Labour Bureau (discontinued 2011); WPI – Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry; CFPI (food inflation) – NSO.

s:
Match List-I (Index) with List-II (Current base year, as of 2026):
List-I | List-II
a. CPI-Combined | i. 2024
b. CPI-IW | ii. 2022-23
c. CPI-AL / CPI-RL | iii. 2016
d. WPI | iv. 2019
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: CPI-Combined – 2024 (replaced 2012); CPI-IW – 2016 (from Sep 2020; earlier 1982, 2001); CPI-AL/RL – 2019 (from June 2025; earlier 1986-87); WPI – 2022-23 (revised 2026; earlier 2011-12).

s:
Consider the following statements about the Labour Bureau and CPI-IW:
1. The Labour Bureau was set up in 1920.
2. It is located at Shimla under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
3. The base year of CPI-IW was revised from 2001 to 2016 with effect from September 2020.
4. CPI-IW is used to fix the dearness allowance of industrial workers and Central Government employees.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Labour Bureau (1920) is at Chandigarh under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, not MoSPI. CPI-IW base: 1982 → 2001 → 2016 (Sep 2020); it is the DA index.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Wholesale Price Index (WPI):
1. Like the CPI, the WPI covers both goods and services.
2. The WPI series with base 2011-12 covered 697 items.
3. In the new WPI (base 2022-23), weights are based on Gross Value Added.
4. The new WPI will run alongside a Producer Price Index for five years, after which the WPI is to be phased out.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: WPI covers goods traded in bulk only – no services (CPI covers goods and services). Statement 3 is wrong: the new WPI (957 items) is weighted on Gross Value of Output, not GVA.

s:
Match List-I (Committee) with List-II (Subject):
List-I | List-II
a. Abhijit Sen | i. WPI base 2004-05
b. Saumitra Chaudhuri | ii. WPI base 2011-12
c. Ramesh Chand | iii. CPI as nominal anchor
d. Urjit Patel | iv. WPI base 2022-23
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Abhijit Sen (2007) – WPI base 2004-05; Saumitra Chaudhuri (2012) – WPI base 2011-12; Ramesh Chand (NITI Aayog, 2025) – WPI base 2022-23; Urjit Patel (2014) – CPI as nominal anchor, flexible inflation targeting.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The GDP deflator is regarded as the broadest measure of inflation.
Reason (R): The GDP deflator covers the prices of all goods and services produced in the economy.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: GDP deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100 covers all goods and services produced, unlike CPI or WPI baskets, so it is the widest measure.

s:
Match List-I (Type of inflation) with List-II (Cause):
List-I | List-II
a. Demand-pull | i. Strong export demand drains domestic supply
b. Cost-push | ii. Poor farm productivity and supply bottlenecks
c. Structural / bottleneck | iii. Rise in wages, raw-material and fuel prices
d. Export-led | iv. Aggregate demand exceeds aggregate supply
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Demand-pull – 'too much money chasing too few goods' (AD > AS); cost-push – rise in factor prices; structural/bottleneck – deficiencies such as poor farm productivity and inefficient storage; export-led – export demand drains domestic supply.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Rising interest rates are a cause of demand-pull inflation.
Reason (R): Rising interest rates reduce aggregate demand.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is false: rising interest rates cut demand, so they do not cause demand-pull inflation (UPSC 2021 key: 1, 2 and 4 only). R is true.

s:
Match List-I (Term) with List-II (Meaning):
List-I | List-II
a. Deflation | i. Inflation returning after deflation
b. Disinflation | ii. Fall in the rate of inflation, which stays positive
c. Reflation | iii. Inflation in some items while others are stable
d. Skewflation | iv. Persistent fall in the general price level
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Deflation – negative inflation; disinflation – e.g. 3% → 2%; reflation – return of inflation after deflation, a sign of recovery; skewflation – inflation in a few items such as food.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Stagflation is a situation of high inflation together with slow growth and high unemployment.
Reason (R): Currency appreciation creates the inflationary half of stagflation.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true (stagflation = high inflation + stagnant output + high unemployment). R is false: a fall in aggregate demand and currency appreciation pull prices down; they do not create inflation.

s:
Consider the following statements about kinds of inflation by speed:
1. Galloping inflation refers to single-digit inflation of 5–9% a year.
2. Creeping inflation is gradual inflation below about 3% a year.
3. Walking or trotting inflation is in the range of 3–10% a year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: galloping inflation is double or triple digit (20%, 100%, 200% a year); 3–10% is walking inflation.

s:
Consider the following statements about supply-side measures against food inflation:
1. The Price Stabilisation Fund, a Central Sector Scheme launched in March 2015, began with onion and potato.
2. Bharat Dal, launched with chana dal in July 2023, was later extended to urad dal.
3. Under OMSS (Domestic), the FCI sells wheat and rice.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct (PSF 2014-15, pulses added later; FCI sells wheat and rice under OMSS). Statement 2 is wrong: Bharat Dal was extended to moong dal, not urad dal; it is sold via NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar.

s:
Consider the following statements about Inflation-Indexed Bonds (IIBs):
1. Their principal and/or interest is linked to an inflation index.
2. They let the government reduce the coupon rate on its borrowing.
3. Interest and capital gains on them are exempt from tax.
4. The RBI issued them in 2013.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct (they protect investors from inflation uncertainty; no inflation-risk premium lowers the coupon; RBI issued IIBs in 2013). Statement 3 is wrong: interest and capital gains on IIBs are taxable (UPSC 2022: A and B only).

s:
Consider the following statements about price monitoring in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The State-level Price Monitoring Committee is headed by the Chief Minister.
2. The Directorate of Economics and Statistics monitors 8 essential commodities daily.
3. Groundnut oil and palm oil were added to the monitored list in February 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the State-level Price Monitoring Committee is headed by the Chief Secretary.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Food inflation is regarded as regressive.
Reason (R): Firms incur menu costs when they repeatedly re-price goods during inflation.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true, but R does not explain A: food inflation is regressive because the poor spend a larger share of income on food; menu costs are a separate cost of inflation borne by firms.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Core inflation excludes volatile food and fuel prices and shows the underlying trend.
2. Headline inflation is more stable than core inflation.
3. Food inflation is measured by the Consumer Food Price Index, which has 10 sub-groups.
4. Cereals carry the highest weight in the Consumer Food Price Index.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: headline inflation includes food and energy and is more volatile; core is more stable.

s:
Match List-I (Inflation fact) with List-II (Period):
List-I | List-II
a. Food > Headline > Core, with AP at 4.9% against India's 3.9% | i. June 2026
b. First breach of the 4% target in the new CPI series (4.38%) | ii. December 2023 – January 2024
c. CPI inflation at a 20-month high of 4.8% | iii. May 2026
d. Retail inflation eased from 5.7% to about 5.1% | iv. August 2026
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: May 2026 – headline 3.93%, food 4.85%, core 3.73%; June 2026 – 4.38%, first breach of 4%; August 2026 – 4.8%, 20-month high; Dec 2023 (5.7%) → Jan 2024 (about 5.1%).

s:
Consider the following statements about flexible inflation targeting in India:
1. The Monetary Policy Framework Agreement between the Government and the RBI was signed in February 2015.
2. The RBI Act, 1934 was amended in 2016 to give inflation targeting a statutory basis.
3. Section 45ZB of the RBI Act provides for the inflation target to be set every five years.
4. Section 45ZN, on reporting after three consecutive quarters of breach, was first invoked in 2022.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the target is set by the Centre with the RBI every five years under Section 45ZA; Section 45ZB provides for the six-member MPC.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Phillips curve:
1. A.W. Phillips (1958) showed an inverse relation between unemployment and wage inflation.
2. Milton Friedman argued that the long-run Phillips curve is horizontal.
3. India's Phillips curve is relatively flat, as about 92% of workers are informal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Friedman held that the long-run Phillips curve is vertical (no lasting trade-off).

s:
Consider the following statements about direct and indirect taxes:
1. Direct taxes are generally progressive in nature.
2. Indirect taxes are generally non-inflationary.
3. Indirect taxes are administered by the CBIC, while direct taxes are administered by the CBDT.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: indirect taxes raise prices and are inflationary; it is direct taxes that are non-inflationary.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Service tax was an indirect tax levied by the Central Government from 1994-95 and was subsumed in GST.
2. The securities transaction tax is an indirect tax because it is collected by the stock exchange.
3. Wealth tax, gift tax and estate duty were called 'paper taxes' because they never yielded much revenue.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: STT (from 1 October 2004) is a direct tax on stock-market transactions, though the exchange collects it.

s:
Consider the following statements about the burden of a tax:
1. The impact of a tax is on the person who finally bears it.
2. Moving the burden of a tax forward to consumers or backward to suppliers is called tax shifting.
3. The burden of property tax cannot be shifted through prices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: impact is on whom the tax is first imposed; the person who finally bears it bears the incidence.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): If the demand for a commodity is perfectly inelastic, the consumer bears the full burden of an indirect tax on it.
Reason (R): When demand elasticity is zero, the price rises by the full amount of the tax.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: with zero elasticity the price rises by the whole tax, so the consumer bears it all; with infinite elasticity the price cannot rise.

s:
Match List-I (Tax) with List-II (Taxable event / base):
List-I | List-II
a. Sales tax / VAT | i. Provision of service
b. Service tax | ii. Supply of goods or services
c. GST | iii. Sale of goods
d. Corporation tax | iv. Net profit of companies
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Sales tax/VAT – sale of goods; service tax – provision of service; GST – supply of goods or services (from 1 July 2017); corporation tax – income/net profit of companies (not production or sales). Central excise is on manufacture, customs on import/export.

s:
Consider the following statements about taxing powers under the Constitution:
1. Article 265 provides that no tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law.
2. The Union List contains 20 taxing entries and the State List 15.
3. The residuary power of taxation rests with Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct (gift, wealth and expenditure taxes were levied under the residuary power). Statement 2 reverses the numbers: Union List 15, State List 20, Concurrent List 3 taxing entries.

s:
Match List-I (Provision) with List-II (Subject):
List-I | List-II
a. Article 276 | i. Surcharges retained by the Union
b. State List Entry 46 | ii. Profession tax, ceiling ₹2,500 a year
c. Article 271 | iii. Agricultural income tax
d. 80th Amendment, 2000 | iv. Sharing of net proceeds of all Union taxes, effective 1 April 1996
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Art. 276 – profession tax (State levy, ceiling ₹2,500 per person per year); State List Entry 46 – agricultural income tax (States only); Art. 271 – surcharges retained by the Union, not shared; 80th Amendment – all Union taxes (minus cess, surcharge) shareable, effective 1 April 1996.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Own tax revenue is the largest component of the revenue receipts of the States.
2. State Excise is the largest source of Andhra Pradesh's own-tax revenue in 2024-25 (RE).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct (own tax about 50% in FY25; tax share about 32%). Statement 2 is wrong: SGST is AP's largest own-tax source (₹36,296 crore, 38%); State Excise is second (22%).

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): VAT is described as a self-enforcing tax.
Reason (R): As a harmonised commodity tax, VAT improves revenue buoyancy.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true, but R does not explain A: VAT is self-enforcing because its invoice-credit trail makes each buyer check the seller's tax; improved buoyancy is a separate merit.

s:
Match List-I (Committee) with List-II (Focus):
List-I | List-II
a. K.N. Raj (1972) | i. Task Forces on direct and indirect taxes
b. L.K. Jha (1976) | ii. Agricultural holding tax
c. Vijay Kelkar (2002) | iii. GAAR and scrapping retrospective tax
d. Parthasarathi Shome (2012) | iv. VAT at the manufacturing stage
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: K.N. Raj – agricultural holding tax; L.K. Jha Indirect Taxation Enquiry Committee (1976) – VAT at manufacturing stage → MODVAT; Vijay Kelkar Task Forces (2002) – both direct and indirect taxes; Parthasarathi Shome (2012) – GAAR, scrap retrospective tax.

s:
Match List-I (Reform) with List-II (Date of introduction):
List-I | List-II
a. MODVAT | i. 1 April 2005
b. CENVAT | ii. 1 March 1986
c. First State VAT (Haryana) | iii. 1 April 2003
d. State VAT nationwide | iv. 1 April 2000
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: MODVAT – 1 March 1986 (Budget 1986-87); CENVAT replaced it on 1 April 2000; Haryana was first with VAT on 1 April 2003; VAT became nationwide (20 States/UTs) on 1 April 2005.

s:
Consider the following statements about service tax:
1. It was introduced in 1994-95 on the advice of the Raja Chelliah Committee.
2. Budget 2015-16 raised its rate from 12% to 14%.
3. From 2012-13 it applied to all services except those in a positive list.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: from 2012-13 service tax applied to all services except those in the negative list.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Union Budget 2026-27 (BE):
1. Direct taxes are about 6.9% of GDP and indirect taxes about 4.3%.
2. Direct taxes make up about 61.2% of gross tax revenue.
3. Income tax is the largest single source of the Centre's receipts in the rupee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: borrowings and other liabilities (24 paise) are the largest receipt; income tax (21 paise) is the largest tax.

s:
Match List-I (Source of the Centre's rupee, Budget 2026-27) with List-II (Share in paise):
List-I | List-II
a. Borrowings and other liabilities | i. 24
b. Income tax | ii. 15
c. Corporation tax | iii. 21
d. GST and other taxes | iv. 18
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Borrowings and other liabilities – 24; income tax – 21; corporation tax – 18; GST and other taxes – 15 (non-tax revenue 10, Union excise 6, customs 4).

s:
Match List-I (Type of tax) with List-II (Feature):
List-I | List-II
a. Progressive | i. Takes a higher proportion of income from low incomes
b. Regressive | ii. One rate for all incomes
c. Proportional | iii. Rate rises at first and then becomes flat
d. Degressive | iv. Rate rises as income rises
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Progressive – rate rises with income (income tax); regressive – higher proportion from low incomes (indirect taxes); proportional – flat rate; degressive – progressive slabs up to a flat top rate.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Laffer curve:
1. It is an inverted-U curve, with zero tax revenue at both 0% and 100% tax rates.
2. The term 'Laffer curve' was coined by Arthur Laffer himself in 1974.
3. It suggests that beyond a certain point higher tax rates may reduce tax revenue.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the curve is associated with Arthur Laffer (1974), but the term was coined by Jude Wanniski.

s:
Match List-I (Levy) with List-II (Key feature):
List-I | List-II
a. Tax | i. Levy for a specific purpose that ends when the purpose is met
b. Fee | ii. Payment for a specific service
c. Cess | iii. Compulsory payment with no quid pro quo
d. Surcharge | iv. Additional charge on the tax payable
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Tax – compulsory, no quid pro quo; fee – quid pro quo for a specific service; cess – 'tax on tax' for a specific purpose; surcharge – additional charge on tax payable, retained by the Union (Art. 271).

s:
Consider the following statements about India's tax-GDP ratio:
1. The Centre's gross tax revenue was 9.9% of GDP in 2019-20.
2. The combined Centre and States tax-GDP ratio is about 19.6%.
3. India's average tax-GDP ratio of 16.36% (2001-22) was the lowest among emerging economies.
4. The World Bank regards a tax-GDP ratio of 20% as the tipping point for sustainable growth.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct (ES 2021-22; States' own tax ≈ 7% of GSDP; below the OECD too). Statement 4 is wrong: the World Bank tipping point is 15%.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Tax buoyancy, unlike tax elasticity, captures the effect of discretionary changes in tax rates and base.
Reason (R): Tax elasticity includes discretionary changes, whereas tax buoyancy excludes them.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true. R is false and reverses the two: buoyancy (% change in revenue / % change in GDP) includes discretionary changes; elasticity excludes them.

s:
Consider the following statements about tax buoyancy:
1. In the 2026-27 BE, gross tax buoyancy is 0.8.
2. In the 2026-27 BE, the buoyancy of indirect taxes (1.1) exceeds that of direct taxes (0.3).
3. According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, buoyant revenues helped bring the fiscal deficit to 4.4% of GDP in FY26.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 reverses the figures: direct-tax buoyancy is 1.1 and indirect-tax buoyancy 0.3.

s:
Match List-I (Committee) with List-II (Focus):
List-I | List-II
a. Nicholas Kaldor (1956) | i. Simplifying the Income-tax Act
b. Wanchoo Committee (1971) | ii. First suggested an expenditure tax
c. Raja J. Chelliah (1991-93) | iii. Black money and tax evasion
d. Justice R.V. Easwar (2015-16) | iv. Lower rates and a broader base; basis of the 1992 wealth-tax revision
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Kaldor – expenditure tax (also wealth, gift, capital gains); Wanchoo (Direct Taxes Enquiry) – black money, evasion; Chelliah – lower rates, broader base, 1992 wealth-tax revision; Easwar – simplifying the Income-tax Act. Agricultural wealth and income taxation was K.N. Raj (1972), not Chelliah.

s:
Consider the following statements about tax task forces:
1. The Kelkar Task Force on FRBM (2004) first proposed a national GST.
2. The task force on a new direct tax law (2017) had Arbind Modi as convener and was later headed by Akhilesh Ranjan, who reported in 2019.
3. The Kelkar Task Forces of 2002 recommended raising the standard deduction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 2002 Kelkar Task Forces recommended abolishing the standard deduction (and wealth tax and Section 88 rebates), with an exemption limit of ₹1 lakh.

s:
Consider the following statements about the history of income tax in India:
1. Income tax was first introduced in 1860 by James Wilson, the first Finance Member.
2. The Income-tax Act, 1961 came into effect on 1 April 1961.
3. The 1997-98 'dream budget' was presented by Yashwant Sinha.
4. The 1997-98 budget cut income-tax rates to 10, 20 and 30%.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 1961 Act took effect on 1 April 1962. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1997-98 dream budget (rates 15/30/40 → 10/20/30%) was P. Chidambaram's.

s:
Match List-I (Income slab under the new regime from Budget 2025-26, unchanged in 2026-27) with List-II (Rate):
List-I | List-II
a. ₹4–8 lakh | i. 5%
b. ₹8–12 lakh | ii. 25%
c. ₹20–24 lakh | iii. 10%
d. Above ₹24 lakh | iv. 30%
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: From Budget 2025-26: 0–4 lakh nil; 4–8 lakh 5%; 8–12 lakh 10%; 12–16 lakh 15%; 16–20 lakh 20%; 20–24 lakh 25%; above 24 lakh 30%. Budget 2026-27 made no slab change.

s:
Consider the following statements about the new income-tax regime:
1. It is the default, exemption-free regime under Section 115BAC.
2. The Section 80C rebate makes income up to ₹12 lakh tax-free.
3. A salaried individual pays no tax up to ₹12.75 lakh because of a standard deduction of ₹75,000.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the rebate is under Section 87A; Section 80C is an old-regime deduction (PPF, NSC, life insurance etc.).

s:
Consider the following statements about the Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT):
1. It was first introduced in Budget 1987-88 under Section 115J.
2. It was withdrawn in 1990 and reintroduced in Budget 1996-97.
3. Budget 2026-27 reduced it to 14% and made it a final tax.
4. New MAT credit continues to be allowed after 1 April 2026.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: from 1 April 2026 no new MAT credit accrues; old credit can be set off up to one-fourth of liability (new regime only). MAT was 15% of book profits before.

s:
Match List-I (Corporate tax option under the Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2019) with List-II (Rate):
List-I | List-II
a. Section 115BAA – base rate | i. About 25.17%
b. Section 115BAA – effective rate | ii. 22%
c. Section 115BAB – base rate | iii. 15%
d. Section 115BAB – effective rate | iv. About 17.01%
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Domestic companies 30% → 22% under Sec 115BAA (effective ~25.17%); new manufacturing companies incorporated after 1 Oct 2019 – 15% under Sec 115BAB (effective ~17.01%); no MAT for those opting in.

s:
Match List-I (Tax) with List-II (Fact):
List-I | List-II
a. Estate duty | i. Abolished in 1985
b. Expenditure tax | ii. Introduced on 1 October 2004
c. Gift tax | iii. Abolished in October 1998
d. Securities transaction tax | iv. Introduced in 1958 by T.T. Krishnamachari
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Estate duty – 1953, abolished 1985; expenditure tax – 1958 (FM T.T. Krishnamachari on Kaldor's advice); gift tax – April 1958, abolished October 1998; STT – 1 October 2004, in force.

s:
Consider the following statements about capital gains tax:
1. As a general rule, a capital asset held for up to 24 months is a short-term capital asset.
2. Indexation uses the Cost Inflation Index notified by the CBDT, with base year 2001-02.
3. Long-term capital gains are taxed at 20% (as of August 2026).
4. Rural agricultural land is a capital asset under the Income-tax Act.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: LTCG is taxed at 12.5%. Statement 4 is wrong: rural agricultural land is not a capital asset.

s:
Consider the following statements about black-money disclosure schemes:
1. The Voluntary Disclosure of Income Scheme was launched in 1997.
2. The Income Declaration Scheme, 2016 (1 June – 30 September 2016) carried a total levy of 45%.
3. The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Yojana, 2016 carried a lower levy than the Income Declaration Scheme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: PMGKY (after demonetisation) carried a 50% levy, higher than the 45% of IDS 2016.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers – Disclosure Scheme (FAST-DS), 2026:
1. Declarants get immunity under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002.
2. It carries a 30% tax plus an equal additional amount, an effective 60%.
3. Its general limit is ₹1 crore, or ₹5 crore for previously taxed but unreported assets on paying a ₹1 lakh fee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: FAST-DS gives immunity under the Black Money Act, 2015.

Consider the following statements about the equalisation levy:
1. A 6% levy on online advertisement services by non-residents was introduced by the Finance Act, 2016.
2. The 6% levy on online advertisements was abolished from 1 April 2024.
3. A 2% levy on e-commerce supplies was imposed in 2020.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 6% levy was abolished from 1 April 2025; it was the 2% e-commerce levy that was dropped in 2024.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Credit for the 2016 equalisation levy could be claimed under Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements.
Reason (R): The equalisation levy was a separate levy, not part of the Income Tax Act.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is false: because the levy was outside the Income Tax Act, no DTAA credit was available. R is true.

s:
Consider the following statements about income-tax administration:
1. Faceless assessment and the Taxpayers' Charter were launched on 13 August 2020.
2. Faceless appeals were launched in September 2020.
3. Project Insight uses artificial intelligence and data analytics for tax compliance.
4. e-Sahyog is a scheme for faceless appeals.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct (Project Insight 2017, working 2019; AIS shows all reported transactions). Statement 4 is wrong: e-Sahyog is an online check of mismatches in returns.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): GST is designed to be non-inflationary.
Reason (R): GST avoids cascading ('tax on tax') through input tax credit.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: by removing tax on tax through input tax credit, GST does not push up prices the way cascading taxes did.

s:
Consider the following statements about the origin of GST in India:
1. GST was first proposed under the Vajpayee government.
2. The Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers was set up in 2000, with Asim Dasgupta as its first chair.
3. The Empowered Committee released 'A Model and Roadmap for GST' in 2008 and its First Discussion Paper in November 2009.
4. The 115th Constitution Amendment Bill on GST, introduced in March 2011, was passed by Parliament.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the 115th Amendment Bill (March 2011) lapsed; GST came through the 122nd Bill (Dec 2014), enacted as the 101st Amendment Act, 2016.

Match List-I (GST event) with List-II (Date):
List-I | List-II
a. 122nd Constitution Amendment Bill tabled | i. 8 July 2017
b. 101st Amendment Act receives Presidential assent | ii. December 2014
c. Jammu and Kashmir adopts GST | iii. 8 September 2016
d. GST 2.0 comes into effect | iv. 22 September 2025
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: 122nd Bill – tabled Dec 2014 (passed by Rajya Sabha Aug 2016); 101st Act – assent 8 Sep 2016; J&K – last to adopt, 8 July 2017; GST 2.0 – 22 Sep 2025.

s:
Consider the following statements about GST:
1. The GST concept was first used in France.
2. India follows the Australian dual-GST model.
3. Amitabh Bachchan was the brand ambassador of GST in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct (France, 1954). Statement 2 is wrong: India follows the Canadian dual model.

s:
Match List-I (Article) with List-II (Content after the 101st Amendment):
List-I | List-II
a. Article 246A | i. GST Council
b. Article 269A | ii. IGST on inter-State trade
c. Article 279A | iii. Simultaneous power to make GST laws; Parliament alone for inter-State supply
d. Article 268A | iv. Service tax – omitted
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: 246A – Parliament and State legislatures both make GST laws, Parliament alone for inter-State supply; 269A – IGST, levied and collected by the Union; 279A – GST Council, constituted by the President; 268A (service tax) – omitted.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The GST constitutional amendment had to be ratified by at least half of the State legislatures.
2. Before GST, VAT was levied under Entry 52 of the State List.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct (federal provisions were touched). Statement 2 is wrong: VAT was a State subject under Entry 54 of the State List.

s:
Consider the following statements about the GST Council:
1. Its first chairperson was Arun Jaitley.
2. The Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance is its Vice-Chairperson.
3. Its Vice-Chairperson is chosen by the State members from among themselves.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct (chair = Union Finance Minister). Statement 2 is wrong: the Union MoS Revenue/Finance is only a member.

s:
Match List-I (GST Council rule) with List-II (Value):
List-I | List-II
a. Quorum | i. One-third of votes cast
b. Weight of the Centre's vote | ii. Three-fourths of weighted votes of members present and voting
c. Weight of all States together | iii. Two-thirds of votes cast
d. Majority for a decision | iv. One-half of total members
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Quorum – one-half of total members; Centre – 1/3 of votes cast; all States together – 2/3 (each State equal); decision – 3/4 majority of weighted votes of members present and voting.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Crude oil, petrol, high-speed diesel, natural gas and aviation turbine fuel are outside the current levy of GST.
Reason (R): These five petroleum products are excluded from GST by Article 366(12A) of the Constitution.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true. R is false: the five petroleum products are within GST constitutionally and will be levied from a date the Council recommends (Art. 279A(5)); only alcoholic liquor for human consumption is excluded by Art. 366(12A).

s:
Consider the following statements about the components of GST:
1. UTGST is levied on intra-UT supplies in Union Territories with a legislature.
2. IGST revenue is finally settled to the destination (consuming) State.
3. The Centre administers and collects CGST and IGST.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: UTGST applies in UTs without a legislature; UTs with a legislature levy SGST.

s:
Consider the following statements about GST rates:
1. GST 2.0 rate rationalisation came into effect on 22 September 2025.
2. Under GST 2.0, the 40% rate applies to sin and ultra-luxury goods.
3. The statutory ceiling for CGST under the GST Acts is 40%.
4. Rates are changed by government notification on the GST Council's recommendation, within statutory ceilings.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct (GST 2.0: 5% merit, 18% standard, 40% sin). Statement 3 is wrong: the CGST ceiling is 20%; 40% is the IGST ceiling.

s:
Match List-I (GST mechanism) with List-II (Meaning):
List-I | List-II
a. Input tax credit | i. Benefit of a rate cut or ITC must reach consumers
b. Reverse charge mechanism | ii. Refund of accumulated input tax credit allowed
c. Anti-profiteering (Section 171, CGST Act) | iii. Tax paid on inputs set off against output tax
d. Inverted duty structure | iv. Liability to pay tax moves from supplier to recipient
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: ITC – input tax set off against output tax; RCM – liability shifts from supplier to recipient; Sec 171 – rate-cut/ITC benefit to be passed on; inverted duty structure – ITC refund.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the GST composition scheme, suppliers of goods with turnover up to ₹1.5 crore pay 1%.
2. Service providers under the composition scheme have a turnover limit of ₹75 lakh and pay 2%.
3. Composition taxpayers cannot claim input tax credit.
4. From 1 October 2024, anti-profiteering cases are heard by the Principal Bench of the GSTAT.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct (anti-profiteering chain NAA → CCI in Dec 2022 → GSTAT from 1 Oct 2024). Statement 2 is wrong: the service-provider limit is ₹50 lakh at 6%.

Consider the following statements:
1. GSTN was set up as a not-for-profit, non-government company in which private institutions held 51%.
2. GSTN was made a fully government-owned company in 2020.
3. An e-way bill is required for movement of goods above ₹50,000.
4. An e-way bill is generally valid for one day for every 200 km.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the decision to make GSTN fully government-owned was taken in 2018 (Centre and States held 24.5% each before).

s:
Consider the following statements about the GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017:
1. It provided compensation to States for five years.
2. It assumed an annual revenue growth of 12% over the base year 2015-16.
3. Any unutilised balance at the end is shared equally between the Centre and the States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct (States' half is divided by their SGST revenue in the last year). Statement 2 is wrong: the assumed growth was 14% a year.

Match List-I (Event) with List-II (Date):
List-I | List-II
a. GST compensation to States ended | i. 31 March 2026
b. Compensation cess scrapped for all goods except tobacco | ii. 1 February 2026
c. Higher excise on tobacco under the Central Excise (Amendment) Act, 2025 | iii. 22 September 2025
d. Compensation cess finally ended | iv. June 2022
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Compensation ended June 2022 (cess continued to repay loans); cess scrapped except on tobacco 22 Sep 2025; higher tobacco excise and the pan-masala cess 1 Feb 2026; cess ended 31 March 2026.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Revenue from the Health Security se National Security Cess on pan masala units is not shared with the States.
Reason (R): The cess is levied on the basis of machine production capacity.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true, but R does not explain A: the cess goes to the Consolidated Fund of India and, being a cess, is outside the divisible pool; the capacity basis only describes how it is assessed.
